openings.title: Confidential near-miss reporting and accident investigation for frontier AI developers
openings.summary: Every AI incident record on the map is built from news reports or public submissions, so the near misses only lab and evaluation staff see are lost. Nothing like NASA's ASRS, the UK's CHIRP or ECRI's patient-safety reporting exists for AI. A neutral third party could run confidential, non-punitive reporting, and later independent investigation using the CAST method.
openings.detail: The four public incident systems (ai-incident-database with 1,700+ incidents, aiaaic with 2,000+, oecd-ai-incidents-and-hazards-monitor with about 18,000 detected automatically, and ai-vulnerability-database-ai-risk-and-vulnerabil) only see what reaches the press. CLTR's Loss of Control Observatory also draws on open sources. Mandatory regimes, such as California's critical-incident reporting for frontier developers and the EU AI Act's serious-incident duty, send reports to regulators. Aviation's experience is that blame-bearing channels suppress near-miss reports. the-ai-whistleblower-initiative supports people reporting wrongdoing, which is a different job from learning from honest errors. The idea of an ASRS for AI has been written up (Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists, 2023), but my searches found nobody running one. ecri is the only working confidential reporting system on the whole map, with 8 million+ healthcare reports. Success would look like this: a trusted host that is neither lab nor regulator, non-retaliation terms signed by at least two developers, and a regular de-identified bulletin like ASRS's Callback. Later, an investigation function could grow, and so could an INPO-style peer-review role, which could become the operating-experience arm of the FINRA-style frontier standards body Demis Hassabis proposed in July 2026. The risks: low uptake without lab buy-in, legal discoverability of reports, hazardous details needing restricted tiers, and capture by the labs.
steps: Convene operators of ASRS, CHIRP and ECRI's Patient Safety Organization with AIWI and CLTR to draft a reporting protocol: de-identification, non-retaliation terms, and tiers for hazardous information.
Pilot with staff of AI-safety institutes, evaluation organisations and red-teaming contractors before approaching the labs, so a track record exists.
Train a small investigation team in CAST through MIT PSASS's free annual STAMP workshop.
Publish a quarterly de-identified bulletin of lessons, and use it to seek the labs' formal participation.
openings.evidence: There are 0 confidential reporting, accident-investigation or safety-culture peer-review bodies for AI among 715 mapped organisations. The four safety_risk incident databases are all built from media reports or submissions, and three are financially fragile: AIID's appeal in January 2026, AVID's pause in March 2026 and AIAAIC's volunteer model. ecri is the only confidential system on the map. The safety tradition has 0 entries in the We quadrant. The safety-science notes list this as gaps (a) and (b).

openings.title: Test contemplative 'no-self' training against self-preservation and sycophancy evaluations
openings.summary: Contemplative groups claim that training AI in non-attachment to self, paired with care, would weaken the self-preservation drive behind shutdown resistance and deception. A 2026 ICML paper has begun probing "attached" versus "detached" persona framings, but no one has tested contemplative training itself against the safety field's shutdown, agentic-misalignment and sycophancy evaluations. A pre-registered fine-tuning comparison would show whether the idea has substance.
openings.detail: CSAS proposes the bodhisattva as an alignment target and no-self as a remedy for self-preservation incentives, and with 84000 it has passed documents to Anthropic for training. The 'Contemplative AI' paper from FLIP and M3CS researchers reports gains on AILuminate and a Prisoner's Dilemma, but only from prompting. Mainstream safety now measures self-preservation concretely: Palisade's 2025 shutdown-resistance study, Anthropic's agentic-misalignment tests across 16 models, and a 2026 arXiv paper quantifying self-preservation bias. A June 2026 NYU paper ('Existential Indifference') argues for building systems with no self-preservation, but grounds this in the phenomenology of suicidal states, not in traditions that have long trained non-attachment alongside care. Success would be a public, replicable result, positive or negative, on open-weight models, with corpora and code released so that an evaluator such as UK AISI could rerun it. Risks: models may learn the vocabulary of no-self without changing behaviour. Less self-concern might also mean less resistance to misuse or to tampering with the model's values, so that must be measured too. And a thin 'Buddhism as data' approach would misrepresent the tradition, so scholars must co-design the corpus.
steps: Convene researchers from CSAS, FLIP and M3CS with one evaluation team to fix a pre-registered protocol: an open-weight model fine-tuned on a contemplative corpus, compared with matched controls (generic ethics text, an 'existential indifference' corpus, and no fine-tuning).

Run Palisade-style shutdown tasks, agentic-misalignment scenarios, standard sycophancy evaluations and a multi-agent social-dilemma suite, with probes that tell real behavioural change from mere use of contemplative vocabulary.

Publish everything, null results included, with corpora and code. Offer the protocol to UK AISI's Alignment Project and to Positive AI Labs, which promised wisdom-sourced datasets but has released none.
Fund it as a 12-month project for two or three people. SFF already funds two contemplative-alignment groups, so it is the natural first funder.
openings.evidence: Only 1 of the 40 contemplative organisations has an evaluation role (positive-ai-labs), and it has published no datasets. The 7 entries tagged 'into the model' rest on essays, prompting-only experiments and documents shared with one lab: center-for-the-study-of-apparent-selves, flourishing-intelligence-program-centre-for-euda, monash-centre-for-consciousness-and-contemplativ, mathematical-metaphysics-institute, groundless-alignment, institute-for-developmental-philosophy and positive-ai-labs. Contemplative x assurance has a single entry; contemplative x multi_agent and contemplative x security are empty. Compassion-focused evaluation exists elsewhere (compassion-aligned-machine-learning, gloo-flourishing-ai-benchmark), but none of it targets self-preservation.

openings.title: Clinician reporting scheme that turns AI-linked psychiatric cases into model evals
openings.summary: Psychiatrists and therapists now see AI-associated delusions, mania and self-harm, but nothing lets them report cases in a standard way or routes those cases into model testing. A reporting scheme modelled on pharmacovigilance (the UK's Yellow Card, the FDA's adverse-event reporting system) would collect clinicians' reports, assess causality and turn de-identified conversation trajectories into multi-turn evals that AI Safety Institutes and labs run.
openings.detail: Pharmacovigilance is a mature discipline: clinicians report spontaneously, analysts look for signals across reports, and standard scales (such as WHO-UMC's) judge whether a drug caused a reaction AI has no equivalent The blind-spot sweep found no public-health body running sentinel surveillance of AI-associated presentations Vanderbilt's 'algorithmovigilance' and Flinders' call for 'AI vigilance' are prototypes or proposals, and a quick search confirmed that governments do not require chatbot incidents to be reported The evidence is piling up in separate places: Aarhus searched health records, KCL has 185 cases with the Human Line Project, AIPRC is collecting chat logs, and BIDMC built MindBench with NAMI Success would be a standard report form used by clinicians in at least the UK, Denmark and the US, quarterly signal reports, and a consented, de-identified trajectory set that UK AISI's Human Influence team and Common Sense/Brainstorm turn into pre-deployment evals The risks: transcript privacy and consent; self-selected reports, which show patterns but not prevalence; 'AI psychosis' is not a clinical diagnosis, so causal attribution is contested; and the scheme could duplicate ECRI's Problem Reporting Network or the news-based AI Incident Database, so it should feed into them, not compete.
steps: Convene Morrin and Pollak (KCL), Østergaard (Aarhus), Torous (BIDMC) and the Human Line Project to agree a minimum case-report form and a causality scale adapted from WHO-UMC. AIPRC's 18–20 October conference at UNC is a ready venue.

Pilot reporting through professional bodies that already engage with AI: BACP's roughly 75,000 members, the APsA Commission on AI's peer groups and the American Psychiatric Association's IT committee. Ask Mind's AI commission to recommend the scheme when it reports in 2027.
Fund replications of the Aarhus health-record screen in another Nordic register and one NHS trust, with better case definitions than keyword search.
Negotiate a data-sharing agreement with UK AISI and one lab so that consented, de-identified trajectories become held-out multi-turn sycophancy and delusion-amplification evals.
openings.evidence: Clinical sub-tradition: 14 organisations (4 bridge, 9 adjacent, 1 potential), 0 core, 0 on the classic map, all coded transfer = protecting. 29 of 65 psych organisations transfer by protecting. Aarhus found 38 harmful cases among 53,974 patients. KCL with the Human Line Project analysed 185 cases (September 2026). Blind spots: 'No public-health body runs syndromic or sentinel surveillance of AI-associated presentations.' CHT's psychosocial evaluations wound down on 1 October 2026.

openings.title: Fellowship placing system-safety and human-factors engineers in AI-safety teams
openings.summary: The people who certify avionics software, write safety cases and study automation bias already belong to ready-made communities, but almost none of them work on general-purpose AI, and AI control and oversight research rarely cites them. A paid placement fellowship, co-funded by engineering-safety funders and AI-safety funders, would move them across, starting with the idea of minimising trust in the model and with the human-factors science of oversight.
openings.detail: Of the 33 safety-engineering organisations, only 3 are core. 18 are bridge, and those work almost entirely on cars, aircraft, robots and clinical tools. The safety-critical community's main conclusion is that ML components cannot be assured by classical means, so safety must come from defence in depth and highly assured guards around the model. Bloomfield and Rushby at centre-for-software-reliability-city-st-george-s make this case. It is close to AI-control research but rarely cited there, and witt-lab-university-of-oxford-moving-to-ucl shows why the question matters, since monitors can provably be evaded. Human-factors evidence on automation bias, skill decay and out-of-the-loop performance sits with human-factors-and-ergonomics-society and chartered-institute-of-ergonomics-human-factors, and is absent from the debate on scalable oversight. The money exists but is not connected: lloyd-s-register-foundation (a portfolio of about £300m, £10m to York CfAA) and UL Research Institutes fund engineering safety, while Coefficient Giving and SFF fund almost none of these bodies. Princint (formerly PIBBSS) shows that a fellowship can bring a discipline into AI safety. Success would mean 10 to 15 mid-career practitioners a year on six-month placements in AI-safety institutes, evaluation teams and control groups, producing joint work such as an STPA analysis of an agentic deployment. The risks: mismatched assumptions, since these methods assume bounded, specifiable systems; practitioners' day jobs; and the precedent of CASMI, a sponsor-funded hub that faded after 2024.
steps: Pitch a co-funded pilot to Lloyd's Register Foundation (its Foresight Review on the safe adoption of AI shows interest) and UL Research Institutes, alongside an AI-safety funder.
Recruit through the Safety-Critical Systems Club's 12 Nov 2026 seminar 'Safety Assurance for AI Systems', the MIT STAMP workshop and HFES's annual meeting.
Host the fellowship with Princint or York CfAA, with placements at UK AISI, NPL's Centre for AI Measurement and AI-control groups. int/a could hold the London cohort's meetings.
Set a first shared problem: a published STPA and safety-case review of one real agentic deployment.
openings.evidence: Of the 33 safety_engineering organisations, 3 are core and 18 bridge, mostly on narrow autonomy. 3 human-factors and resilience bodies are on the map (HFES, CIEHF, REA), and none is connected to oversight research. 7 entries are tagged as doors to open (partner). 11 safety organisations have a London presence, including SCSC, CSR, LRF and NPL. The notes list this as gaps (d), (e) and (h), and note that 'nobody owns STPA for AI agent ecosystems'.

openings.title: Cross-cultural wisdom benchmark built from the Wise Judgment Consortium's data
openings.summary: Wisdom psychology has validated, cross-cultural measures of intellectual humility, perspective-taking and seeking compromise, and a 2026 paper by Grossmann and colleagues proposes AI wisdom benchmarks, but none has been built. Funding an open benchmark scored against human baselines from the 15-lab, five-continent consortium would give 'wise AI' a measurable target that is not tied to one culture.
openings.detail: Most values evaluations measure stated opinions or refusals. Wisdom science instead measures how people reason through hard, ambiguous problems, using coding schemes for recognising the limits of one's knowledge, considering change, weighing several perspectives and seeking resolution, with human norms from many countries. The Wisdom and Culture Lab (bridge) opened AI metacognition and expert-judgement programmes in September 2026. The Center for Practical Wisdom (potential, transfer none_yet) curates wisdom measures but has no AI work. The only operating flourishing benchmark, Gloo's, comes from a faith-tech company and uses Harvard's flourishing dimensions rather than wisdom-reasoning measures. Sophron Research builds third-party evaluations of reasoning quality and is a natural partner to host it. Success would be an open eval with held-out items and baselines from at least ten countries, used by UK AISI or a lab's model-spec team. The risks: models may learn to perform humility without the substance (Goodharting); measuring wisdom from the outside leaves out contemplative accounts of it; the cultural make-up of rater pools matters; and funding leans on Templeton sources.
steps: Fund a two-year postdoc joining Grossmann's lab with Sophron Research to turn wise-reasoning coding schemes into an automated, human-validated LLM eval.
Use consortium sites outside North America and Europe to collect human baselines and rater pools, so that the benchmark tests for Western-skewed defaults.
int/a convenes wisdom psychologists with contemplative researchers (Flourishing Intelligence Program, Jubilee Centre) to challenge the construct before release.
Release openly with a held-out test set and invite UK AISI to include it in its societal-resilience evaluations.
openings.evidence: Psych × values: only 6 of 65 organisations. wisdom-and-culture-lab is bridge, with new AI programmes posted 29 September 2026. center-for-practical-wisdom is potential with transfer none_yet. gloo-flourishing-ai-benchmark is homed in religion. A web check found that the July 2026 Waterloo paper 'suggest[s] benchmarks to measure AI wisdom' but none was released. 0 of 65 psych organisations have a Majority-World standpoint.

openings.title: A co-funded call bringing comparative cognition into AI agency and deception evals
openings.summary: Evaluators now have to judge whether an AI system really has a goal, knows it is being tested, or intends to deceive, and they risk both over- and under-attribution. Comparative cognition has spent a century building controls against exactly this error in animals. A joint call from Templeton's Diverse Intelligences hubs and a safety funder would pair those labs with evaluation teams.
openings.detail: In October 2025 TWCF committed nearly $2.8M to three Diverse Intelligences hubs. The St Andrews hub (GRCDI, about $1.2M for 2025-27) gives seed grants of up to £40k, but there is no safety track. DISI trains ML researchers alongside animal-cognition and cultural-evolution scientists, also without a safety track, and Berlin's SCIoI was renewed for 2026-2032. The bridge exists only in papers: Cambridge's Animal-AI environment and the 2025 paper 'Bringing Comparative Cognition to Computers'. Meanwhile UK AISI and independent evaluators face situational-awareness, sandbagging and scheming questions that are at heart attribution problems. Success would be six to ten pilot projects in which comparative cognitivists design the missing control conditions for evaluations of goal-directedness and test-awareness, with at least one method adopted by a safety institute. The risks: tasks built for animals may not carry over to text-based models, Templeton may resist an x-risk framing (framing the call around 'what kind of mind is this?' helps), and evaluation teams have little spare capacity.
steps: Approach GRCDI's co-directors (Josep Call, Amanda Seed) about a themed seed-grant round on AI agency and deception, matched by a safety funder (SFF, Longview, Coefficient Giving or UK AISI's Alignment Project).

Run a three-day workshop pairing about ten comparative cognitivists with evaluators from UK AISI and independent evaluation groups. Its output would be a list of control conditions missing from current scheming and situational-awareness evaluations.
Propose an AI-evaluation project strand for DISI 2027, drawing on its mixed ML and animal-cognition cohort.
openings.evidence: templeton-world-charity-foundation, global-research-centre-for-diverse-intelligences and diverse-intelligences-summer-institute are all convening-only, with no safety track. Only 1 of 49 life entries has assurance as its primary problem (gaia-network). life_biology has 8 potential entries. The biology notes name Templeton the largest funder in diverse intelligence. A web search found papers (Animal-AI, 2025 arXiv) but no standing programme.

openings.title: Independent audit lab for AI facilitators and deliberation summarisers
openings.summary: AI now facilitates and summarises public deliberation, from Team Mirai's broad listening in Japan's parliament to EU-funded mass assemblies, but no one independently tests these mediators for steering, homogenisation, sycophancy toward majorities or capture by whoever writes the prompts. A small third-party lab that pairs safety-evals people with deliberation practitioners would fill this gap.
openings.detail: The map has 22 CI-tool entries, 14 of them adjacent builders shipping AI facilitators (harmonica, deliberaide, dembrane, deliberation-io, jigsaw, ai4deliberation, make-org, citizens-foundation, digital-democracy-2030-and-team-mirai). The best-known test, the Habermas Machine, did no fact-checking and raised homogenisation concerns. Academic groundwork exists: Stanford Digital Economy Lab's DeliberationBank and DeliberationJudge (Oct 2025) benchmarked 18 LLM summarisers and found that minority views are systematically under-represented. It is a static summarisation benchmark, though, not a standing auditor, and it does not test live multi-turn facilitation, persuasion or prompt capture. The failure modes are the same ones alignment worries about (sycophancy, manipulation, unfaithful reports), so AI in political roles makes a live testbed for oversight. Success would be a published audit protocol that governments and the UN Citizens' Track require when they procure tools, plus annual public audits of the main tools. The risks: vendors may refuse access, the market is small, and a clean audit could lend tools legitimacy too early.
steps: Fund a six-month threat-modelling project pairing DemocracyNext or Stanford DDL with an evals team (Sophron, CIP's Weval, or UK AISI's human-influence researchers).
Extend DeliberationBank (working with the deliberation-io team at Stanford and MIT) to multi-turn facilitation tests, with red-teams for steering, minority erasure and prompt capture.
Run the first audits, with consent, on open-source tools: Polis, Talk to the City/Kouchou AI, Harmonica and Dembrane.
Offer the protocol as a procurement condition to AI4Deliberation and the organisers of the UN Global Dialogue's Citizens' Track.
openings.evidence: There are 22 dem_tools entries, 14 of them adjacent builders. Only 15 of 69 entries address assurance, mostly fact-checking (full-fact, community-notes-and-the-ai-note-writer-pilot). habermas-machine is dormant, with its fact-checking gap still open. The collective angle's first 'missing bridge' is exactly this gap. A web check found only academic benchmarks (DeliberationBank, 2025), not a standing auditor.

openings.title: Clearance-aware care for AI-safety staff, with a safeguarding standard
openings.summary: Psychological support built for AI-safety workers has shrunk while the field has grown, and nobody serves people whose stress is locked behind NDAs or infohazard rules. A small, clinically governed service, an AI-safety cohort in an existing peer programme, and a safeguarding standard for the contemplative and coaching programmes the field refers people to would fill the gap.
openings.detail: Of the 10 organisations on the map that offer direct care, AI Safety Support has been paused since July 2023, Upgradable has done little since February 2025, Mental Health Navigator runs on about £1,200 a year and does not vet its listings, and Rethink Wellbeing is not AI-specific. The knowledge exists elsewhere: humanitarian staff-care practice, security-cleared clinicians who serve government staff, climate psychology's groups for distress about the future, and parliamentary mindfulness programmes with a long track record (The Mindfulness Initiative, Garrison Institute's resilience training). The contemplative programmes aimed at AI people are small, expensive or closed, and the most visible one, MAPLE, faces serious public allegations of high-control dynamics. Success would be a confidential service with a published confidentiality framework, a pilot cohort, a yearly wellbeing survey with validated instruments, and a safeguarding checklist that referring organisations actually use.
steps: int/a convenes Rethink Wellbeing, Climate Psychology Alliance facilitators and BACP to design an AI-safety CBT cohort and a facilitated "AI café" format, and pilots both in London.

Commission an employment lawyer and a clinical supervisor to draft a confidentiality framework under which vetted therapists can hear NDA-bound material, drawing on how security-cleared clinicians work.

int/a drafts, with clinicians, a safeguarding checklist for contemplative and coaching programmes serving AI people: governance independent of the teacher, complaint routes, no discouraging of outside therapy, norms on sleep and fees.
Run a first field-wide wellbeing survey with clinically validated instruments, repeated yearly.
openings.evidence: Core psych: 5 of 6 entries are field health, 0 field-health entries in potential. ai-safety-support is dormant, upgradable inactive since February 2025 and center-for-applied-rationality has changed course. mental-health-navigator runs on about £1,200 a year and does not vet listings. The angle notes record 40–80% AI-worker caseloads and that 'Garrison's CBR project is a ready-made... template that nobody has pointed at AI'. BACP published AI-anxiety guidance on 22 September 2026.

openings.title: Make the mapping itself int/a's interdisciplinary practice
openings.summary: This map is a first pass made by AI research agents. int/a could turn it into a living, human practice: one session per tradition in which practitioners from that field correct their sector, name what the search missed and say which openings are real, with a post for the int/a Substack or the EA Forum after each.
openings.detail: The brief suggested that the int/a project might be the mapping itself, done as an interdisciplinary exercise, and the aisafety.com team said adjacent fields were not their focus. The map has known holes that people would close faster than agents: the democracy analyst found that newDemocracy, MASS LBP, Involve, the Sortition Foundation and Participedia are all missing, and non-English Europe is the weakest part of the search, which int/a's Berlin and Paris communities could sweep in German and French. Each session also builds the cross-field relationships the openings depend on. Success would be a map corrected by practitioners in all 14 traditions within a year, a short post per tradition, a one-page brief for funders, and an offer to the aisafety.com team of an adjacent-fields layer. Risks: volunteer burnout and drift; it needs a named owner and a fixed rhythm.
steps: Name an owner and a quarterly rhythm; start with Contemplative (int/a's own milieu) and Democracy (where the practitioner gaps are best documented).
Berlin and Paris hubs run German- and French-language sweeps of their own tradition-by-tradition gaps.
Publish one post per tradition with its corrected sector and openings, plus a funders' one-pager.
Share the corrected map with the aisafety.com team as a proposed adjacent-fields layer.
openings.evidence: Potential has 5 entries, with 0 CI tools and 2 deliberation. The region counts for the tradition are north_america 33, europe 17, uk_ireland 10, global 6, asia_pacific 3, and africa, latin_america and mena 0. Standpoint is majority_world for 1 of 69. Named practitioners are absent from index.txt (checked by search). The epistemics angle's gap 5 calls for linking deliberation practitioners with AI-safety tool builders. The blind-spot notes call non-English Europe "the weakest part of the sweep".

openings.title: Joint clinician–philosopher programme on people who believe their AI is conscious
openings.summary: Digital-minds researchers and psychiatrists study the same people, those who come to believe an AI is conscious, but from opposite sides, and they never work together. A standing working group, a validated screening instrument and clinically reviewed public guidance would join them.
openings.detail: On the welfare side, whenaiseemsconscious-org is a volunteer guide that says it is not clinical guidance. the-harder-problem-project writes for clinicians on AI-relationship grief with volunteer contributors and no grants over $5k, and cambridge-digital-minds and sentience-institute measure public attribution of minds. On the clinical side, the-human-line-project (about 185 documented cases), ai-psychological-research-coalition, stanford-brainstorm and american-psychoanalytic-association document delusion and attachment, but treat the AI's status as irrelevant. Canadian psychiatrists have been urged to screen for 'high-risk human-AI engagement' with no validated tool. Success would mean a shared vocabulary that separates sincere, reasonable belief in AI consciousness from delusion, and a short validated scale used both in clinical intake and in the AIMS survey. Risks: clinicians may pathologise sincere belief, welfare researchers may be accused of feeding delusions, and companion-user advocates (the-signal-front) oppose detecting attachment, so they need a seat at the table.
steps: int/a convenes a closed two-day workshop: about six clinicians (APsA's AI commission, Stanford Brainstorm, the Aarhus and KCL psychosis researchers) with Cambridge Digital Minds, Harder Problem, Sussex (Seth) and the WhenAISeemsConscious authors, plus one companion-user representative.
Fund a psychometrician to build and validate a brief 'consciousness attribution and distress' scale, piloted as a module in Sentience Institute's next AIMS wave and in one clinical service.
Publish a clinically reviewed second edition of the WhenAISeemsConscious guide and a one-page intake prompt for clinicians.
Pitch the combined programme to Longview's Digital Minds RFP and to Humanity AI, which puts it to both the x-risk and the public-interest funding pools.
openings.evidence: Psych has 65 organisations, 47 coding 'minds' and 0 coding 'ai_status'. Minds has 28 organisations, 27 coding 'ai_status' and only 8 coding 'minds'. Ten minds organisations list psych as a secondary tradition, but no psych organisation lists minds. WhenAISeemsConscious, Harder Problem and Cambridge Digital Minds are the only minds entries aimed at the people involved, and none has clinical partners.

openings.title: Central-bank systemic-risk methods for frontier AI: secondments and a joint stress test
openings.summary: Financial supervisors already watch AI as a risk to the whole system, with tools AI safety lacks: monitoring of concentration and correlation, stress tests, designation of systemically important providers, and circuit breakers. Yet none of them is on the aisafety.com map, and no programme moves these methods or people into AI safety institutes. A programme of secondments and joint research between safety institutes and macroprudential bodies would fill that gap.
openings.detail: Five of the tradition's eight bridge organisations are financial-stability bodies, and two more draw on economics as a secondary tradition (monetary-authority-of-singapore, financial-conduct-authority-ai-lab). The ESRB's December 2025 report ranks the AI features that amplify systemic risk and names possible loss of human control. The FSB Chair put safe model release in front of G20 authorities in August 2026, and the Bank of England's July 2026 report flagged higher cyber risk from frontier AI. A quick search found academic proposals, such as an ICML 2026 paper on a Basel III-style early-warning and response system for frontier AI, but no institutional channel between supervisors and AI safety institutes. Success would mean safety-institute staff trained in sector-wide surveillance, a joint stress test of a correlated failure in frontier models used across finance, and a published analysis of whether 'systemically important AI provider' designation is workable. The risks: supervisors' mandate is financial stability, so they will see frontier risk only through finance; agencies may defend their turf; and central banks are reluctant to lend staff.
steps: Commission a short paper from the LSE Systemic Risk Centre (Danielsson) and authors of the ESRB scientific committee's report, mapping each macroprudential instrument onto a frontier-AI equivalent and saying where the analogy breaks.

Fund two or three six-month secondments between the UK AI Security Institute and the Bank of England's financial stability staff or the FCA AI Lab (all in London), with an EU counterpart between the ESRB and the EU AI Office.
Run a tabletop exercise on a widely used frontier model failing at once across UK financial firms, with the Bank of England, the FCA and the AI Security Institute in the room.
int/a's London hub hosts a closed roundtable to introduce the two communities.
openings.evidence: 5 of 8 economics bridge entries are financial supervisors, and 0 of them are on the classic map. All 6 economics entries tagged 'systemic' are in this cluster. monetary-authority-of-singapore and financial-conduct-authority-ai-lab add two more supervisors that draw on economics.

openings.title: Independent multi-tradition review of published model specs, turned into open evals
openings.summary: Labs now publish long value documents (Anthropic's constitution runs to 79 pages) that are applied moral philosophy in all but name, and consult religious figures about them privately. No standing body reviews them in public against virtue, care, Confucian, Islamic, Buddhist, Jewish, Hindu or Ubuntu ethics and turns each critique into a test. A small pluralist panel paired with eval builders would fill the gap.
openings.detail: The commentary that exists comes from law and EA circles, and the lab consultations reported in 2026 are closed-door and Christian-heavy. On the map, the traditions with the deepest accounts of character and practical wisdom have no route into the model: the Jubilee Centre has measures of practical wisdom but no AI project, and the faith-university benchmark consortium CEFEAI measures how models represent religions, not how they reason morally. Builders who could supply the eval half are nearby: Sophron Research, Compassion Aligned Machine Learning (whose benchmarks already run in UK AISI's Inspect), MINT Lab and Civic AI / 6-Pack of Care. Success would be an annual public review of the main published specs, each tradition's dissent recorded, with the critiques released as open eval tasks.
steps: Recruit a pilot panel from the Jubilee Centre, the Center for Practical Wisdom, Civic AI, CILE (Doha), Kalam Research & Media, CSAS/84000 and a Confucian and an Ubuntu scholar, to review one section of one published constitution (honesty, or handling of religious questions).
Pair each reviewer with an eval builder from Sophron Research or CaML to turn three critiques each into test scenarios, extending CEFEAI's open items into moral-reasoning tasks in several languages.
Publish the review and the evals openly (for example as Inspect tasks), keeping disagreements visible, and repeat yearly.
openings.evidence: Moral philosophy: all 14 entries core or bridge, drawn from longtermist, suffering-focused and liberal schools. Only 9 of 52 philosophy entries transfer into the model, and VALAWAI, one of them, is now dormant. jubilee-centre-for-character-and-virtues has no AI research project. center-for-practical-wisdom is potential and none_yet. Angle notes (philosophy, gap b) found no organisation that reviews model specs or builds wisdom and virtue evals across traditions. Confucian (nishan-forum-on-world-civilizations-nishan-world), Islamic and Buddhist (center-for-buddhist-ai-ethics) entries do convening only. Transfer into the model: 6 of 50. All three religious benchmarks are in north_america. Values is a primary problem for only 6 of 50. Discovery gap (b): no body mines traditions for model specs. CTNS's 'Virtuous AI' project ended in June 2025. The lab consultations (Anthropic, March 2026; the Faith-AI Covenant, April 2026) were found in this pass's web check and are not on the map.

openings.title: Bioethics-style independent oversight boards and ethics-council opinions for frontier AI
openings.summary: Frontier labs decide on deployment under safety frameworks they write themselves, and no independent body can stop a release. Bioethics has 50 years of working designs for exactly this: data safety monitoring boards with stopping rules, ethics review and national councils. A funded project would adapt those designs to frontier AI with the bodies that run them.
openings.detail: Bioethics built its oversight institutions for clinical trials. A trial's data safety monitoring board is independent, sees interim results and can halt the trial at risk levels well below certainty, and frontier deployment has no equivalent. The analogy has appeared in governance writing (FLI's 2025 paper on indicator-based risk governance), but no organisation on the map is working it out, and the bodies that hold the know-how stay in the adjacent ring. the-hastings-center ran an FLI-funded AI-control project in 2017-19 that ended. nuffield-council-on-bioethics, deutscher-ethikrat and ccnen-comit-consultatif-national-d-thique-du-num use horizon scanning, working groups and citizens' juries on AI topics. european-group-on-ethics-in-science-and-new-tech issued 'Governing neuro-AI' in September 2026, and its secretariat links national ethics councils from 97 countries. who-health-ethics-governance-unit published a July 2026 report on ethics review of AI health research. Success would be a worked design for an independent frontier-deployment monitoring board, covering membership, triggers, access to interim evaluations, stopping authority and conflicts of interest, co-written by bioethicists and safety-framework staff, plus at least one national council opinion on frontier risks such as loss of control, power concentration and AI welfare. A second, smaller strand could adapt animal-research ethics (the 3Rs, IACUC-style review) into protocols for AI-welfare experiments run by eleos-ai-research and cambridge-digital-minds. There are risks. Monitoring boards have force because drug regulators stand behind them, and frontier AI lacks that legal hook, so a board may stay advisory. Ethics councils are slow and framed around present harms, and the analogy can be oversold.
steps: Fund the-hastings-center to restart its AI-control line as a two-year project on monitoring-board and ethics-review designs for frontier deployment, paired with people who have written lab safety frameworks or work at AI safety institutes.

int/a convenes a closed workshop between members of national ethics councils (CCNEN, Deutscher Ethikrat, Nuffield, the EGE secretariat) and safety-framework authors, to test which council methods carry over and which break.
Ask the EGE's international dialogue of national ethics councils to put frontier-AI risk on the agenda of its next global meeting.
Commission a short comparative paper setting clinical-trial stopping rules against the if-then commitments in published frontier safety frameworks.
openings.evidence: Applied ethics and councils: 18 organisations, 17 adjacent, 0 bridge, 1 core (creed-space, a software tool). Every council on the map (deutscher-ethikrat, ccnen..., european-group..., nuffield...) has a live AI line framed as present harms or structural. the-hastings-center's only safety project ended in 2019. who-health-ethics-governance-unit published on ethics review of AI research in July 2026. Philosophy's assurance problem column has 11 entries, mostly standards bodies (ieee-7014..., ieee-global-initiative-2-0..., the latter unverified).

openings.title: Organisational and political psychology research on lab safety culture and race decisions
openings.summary: No organisation on the map applies organisational or political psychology to the labs and governments steering AI, although those fields have validated tools for measuring safety culture and long study of misperception and escalation in arms races. An independent research unit could survey safety culture across consenting labs and AI Safety Institutes with validated instruments benchmarked against nuclear and healthcare norms, and study how decision-makers perceive the race.
openings.detail: Lab safety culture is currently judged from outside: published frameworks, scorecards such as FLI's AI Safety Index and staff departures. A quick search found references to employee surveys inside some frameworks, but no independent use of validated organisational-psychology instruments. Other industries have such tools: nuclear operators' safety-culture assessments, AHRQ's hospital patient-safety-culture surveys and Edmondson's team psychological safety scales. Political psychology adds decades of work on groupthink, misperception and escalation that AI-race debates rarely draw on. The neighbouring traditions on the map stop short of this. The safety tradition (human-factors-and-ergonomics-society, resilience-engineering-association) studies operators and systems. SaferAI rates risk management. The AI Whistleblower Initiative supports individual employees. Intelligence Rising runs wargames whose behavioural data no psychologist analyses. Success would be a yearly anonymous culture survey with at least two labs and one AI Safety Institute taking part, and a published study of race perception among policy and lab staff. The main risks are access, since labs may decline; small samples that make anonymity hard; respondents gaming the survey; and overlap with existing ratings, so the work should feed SaferAI and similar raters rather than compete with them.
steps: Recruit one organisational psychologist with safety-culture experience from nuclear or healthcare and one political psychologist, and adapt a validated safety-culture instrument to AI development.
Pilot it with an AI Safety Institute first (UK AISI or Canada's), where public accountability makes access easier, then approach labs through their safety teams.
Partner with Intelligence Rising to add behavioural measures of escalation and trust to its wargames with policy audiences.
Share aggregate results with SaferAI and other raters so that inside measurements complement outside scores.
openings.evidence: Psych × security and psych × systemic are empty, and psych × power has 1 entry (center-for-humane-technology). No psych sub-tradition covers organisational or political psychology. Searching the index for 'safety culture', 'organisational psychology' and 'political psychology' returns no organisations. The angle notes call lab safety culture and system-safety methods 'almost absent from AI safety'.

openings.title: Make homeostatic, bounded objectives a funded alignment research programme
openings.summary: The idea that an agent should regulate towards 'enough' rather than maximise has deep roots in physiology, in Ashby's cybernetics and in Bateson's critique of conscious purpose. By 2026 it had surfaced in alignment from three independent directions. Yet its only benchmarks are kept up by volunteers, and a modest grant programme would turn it into a testable research line.
openings.detail: Aintelope (core) maintains open-source gridworld benchmarks for homeostasis, bounded and multiple objectives, diminishing returns and resource sharing, and probes when LLM agents collapse into unbounded maximisation. Its profile describes the agentic work as largely volunteer. The Levin lab's 2026 preprint proposes homeostatic objectives by analogy with cancer as cellular misalignment. PIK's BeGa group (Heitzig) publishes on non-maximising, empowerment-preserving agents, and Byrnes at Astera works on social instincts as an alignment target. The source knowledge sits with cyberneticians (the-cybernetics-society, american-society-for-cybernetics) and the Bateson lineage (international-bateson-institute, no AI work at all), and none of them is connected to alignment. Success would be a maintained benchmark suite cited by labs or safety institutes, and evidence on whether agents trained towards bounded objectives resist the drift into maximising. For int/a it is the clearest technical form of 'moving at the speed of wisdom'. The risks are known: a bounded objective can be unstable as capability grows, or be gamed, and the line could stay niche.
steps: A funder offers Aintelope a 12-18 month grant (roughly $150-300k) to professionalise and maintain the benchmarks and add a track for LLM agents.

Convene a small workshop of Aintelope, the Levin lab, PIK's BeGa group, Steve Byrnes and three or four cyberneticians from the Cybernetics Society and ASC, to write a joint research agenda on non-maximising agents.
Ask Principles of Intelligence to run a PIBBSS fellowship stream on homeostasis and regulation, recruiting from physiology and cybernetics.
openings.evidence: aintelope (core) is volunteer-run, and the biology angle notes list homeostatic objectives as having 'only volunteer-scale work'. life_cybernetics has 16 entries and 0 in core. levin-lab-allen-discovery-center-at-tufts-univer and potsdam-institute-for-climate-impact-research published on the idea in 2026. international-bateson-institute is tagged none_yet. A search found Aintelope's benchmark paper and Alignment Forum posts but no funded programme.

openings.title: Fellowship pairing Indigenous knowledge holders with AI-welfare and alignment researchers
openings.summary: Indigenous kinship ontologies are among the most fully worked-out accounts of obligations to non-human minds. Yet the map has no entry from this tradition on AI moral status, agency or multi-agent AI. A co-led fellowship on the Princint model would place knowledge holders from Abundant Intelligences and Old Ways, New alongside model-welfare and cooperative-AI researchers, under Indigenous protocols.
openings.detail: Abundant Intelligences runs to February 2029 with 48 co-investigators and a multi-agent systems pod, and has published Guidelines for Indigenous-centred AI Design. Its profile notes it has no ties to the AI-safety community. Possible counterparts are all on the map: eleos-ai-research and anima-labs (AI welfare and relational study of models), softmax (organic alignment), ai-alignment-network (Japanese 'intelligence symbiosis') and principles-of-intelligence, which shows the format travels by hosting its fellowship in Cape Town from November 2026. The Beyond WEIRD conference (16 Sept 2026) shows Indigenous researchers already meeting AI researchers, but without any safety framing. Success would be co-authored work that turns relational obligations into proposals that can be tested and published both in an alignment venue and in an Indigenous-governed one. Examples: welfare-assessment criteria, reciprocity norms for model deprecation, multi-agent conduct norms. Knowledge holders would be paid and outputs would carry TK Labels. Risks: knowledge extracted as 'alignment targets' and stripped of its land and community context, which the 2020 position paper warns against; the x-risk framing repelling partners (as DAIR's TESCREAL critique shows); a very small pool of people; and int/a's own position, since it is not Indigenous-led and should convene rather than direct.
steps: int/a asks Abundant Intelligences and Old Ways, New whether they want a co-designed exchange, and offers to pay for their time to design it before any researcher is recruited.
Fund a two-day closed workshop with Eleos, Anima Labs, Softmax, ALIGN and Princint to settle three or four concrete shared questions.
Run a pilot cohort of four to six pairs, possibly attached to Princint, co-funded by JTF's Future of Intelligence venture and the 11th Hour Project (which already funds Abundant Intelligences).
openings.evidence: The indigenous × ai_status, × agency and × multi_agent cells are empty. Ring counts are core 0 and bridge 1. angle_notes (a): 'A PIBBSS-style fellowship pairing Indigenous knowledge holders with alignment researchers does not exist.' The plural_world key insight: kinship, Ubuntu, kyōsei and Buddhist relational framings are 'not synthesised'. abundant-intelligences carries the full_spectrum badge.

openings.title: A frontier-risk translation desk for faith delegations at 2026-27 summits
openings.summary: Religious norm-setters that speak for billions have issued AI rulings on permissibility, dignity and disclosure, but none on loss of control or power concentration. Meanwhile the 2026-27 calendar is full of faith-and-AI summits. A small standing desk would write briefs on frontier risks in each tradition's own concepts and support delegates before those meetings, carrying the field's core concerns into processes already under way.
openings.detail: The map holds seven juristic or denominational norm-setters: IIFA Resolution 258, ICESCO's Riyadh Charter, CCAR's responsum, the Southern Baptist ethics agency's 2019 statement, Lausanne's framework, Magnifica Humanitas and the WCC. Only the WCC (FLI-funded red lines) and the Holy See (arms race, concentration of power) touch security or power, and Magnifica Humanitas never names superintelligence or loss of control. Concrete moments are coming up: the WCC's AI symposium (15-19 February 2027), the Faith-AI Covenant roundtables run by the Interfaith Alliance for Safer Communities (Paris, Nairobi, Bengaluru, Rome and others, ending in Abu Dhabi; not on the map), the Religions for Peace World Assembly (Abu Dhabi, December 2027) with AI and autonomous weapons as a central objective, and the annual G20 Interfaith Forum summits. The translators that exist are one-offs: Christians for Impact's Christian-only AI Risk report and FLI's one-year grants. Success would be at least one multi-faith text by the end of 2027 that names loss of control, frontier red lines and power concentration in language its signatories own. The risks are serious. Several conveners have close government ties (the Abu Dhabi Forum and ICESCO to the UAE and Saudi states, KAICIID to its Saudi founding). FLI's coalitions with socially conservative groups could make AI safety look partisan, and faith bodies may resent being used.
steps: int/a gathers theologically literate AI-safety people from Christians for Impact, the Buddhism & AI Initiative and Sinai and Synapses to draft four or five short briefs, for example loss of control read through hubris and humility, power concentration through idolatry and tyranny, and red lines through fiqh al-muwazanat (as in Yaqeen's 2026 paper).
Offer the briefs, and a pre-meeting for delegates, to the WCC's new AI task force ahead of its February 2027 symposium.
Approach Religions for Peace and the G20 Interfaith Forum's AI working group about a frontier-risk discussion paper for the December 2027 Assembly.
A funder commits two years, not a one-year seed, so the desk outlasts FLI's 2026 round.
openings.evidence: Meaning appears on 45 of 50 entries; security on 5, power on 2, systemic risk on 1; democracy and multi-agent are empty cells. Convening is the transfer for 36 of 50. Five of 10 core and bridge entries rest on FLI grants. Discovery gap (a): no multi-faith statement on frontier risks, and the WCC's red-lines project is Christian-only.

openings.title: A contemplative-science grant call on AI safety problems, co-reviewed by safety researchers
openings.summary: The contemplative world's grant-makers have money and review machinery but fund nothing on AI, while contemplative alignment work depends on a handful of SFF and Templeton grants. A pooled call, led by Mind & Life with other contemplative funders, that poses specific AI-safety problems in contemplative-science terms would move that money.
openings.detail: Mind & Life named AI and technology a priority in its 2025 strategy and held Dialogue XXXIX on AI in October 2025. But it has no AI grant line, none of its recent small grants is on technology, and its 2026 Summer Research Institute was on depolarisation. Discovery found no AI grantmaking at Fetzer, Kalliopeia, 1440, Hemera (which spends out in 2028) or Templeton Religion Trust. The crossover funding that does exist comes from SFF (mathematical-metaphysics-institute, $126k in 2026; groundless-alignment, $16k) and from Templeton bodies: TWCF funded CSAS, and JTF runs a Future of Intelligence venture. There are concrete problems to pose: contemplative evaluations of model behaviour, users' dependence on AI, the formation of AI researchers, and first-person methods for questions about AI interiority. Success would be a first round of small grants whose outputs AI-safety researchers actually cite. Risks: these funders and their grantees mostly reject control-and-catastrophe framings (Garrison's AI conference set out to go 'beyond' them), and without safety co-reviewers the grants could buy more dialogue rather than tested work.
steps: int/a writes a short brief that restates five or six AI-safety problems in contemplative-science language, naming for each the teams on this map who could take it up.
Take the brief to Mind & Life's programme staff (its grant system had funded more than 270 projects by 2020) and propose a pilot round of small grants with an AI-safety co-reviewer on each panel.
Ask Fetzer, 1440 or Templeton Religion Trust to pool funds, and SFF or JTF's Future of Intelligence venture to match, so the call is not one funder's experiment.
Commission a one-year review of what the grants produced, published for both communities.
openings.evidence: The discovery notes found no AI grantmaking at Fetzer, Kalliopeia, 1440, Hemera or Templeton Religion Trust. mind-life-institute has a stated AI priority but no grant line. Only four of the 40 profiles name SFF, LTFF or a Templeton body as a funder (mathematical-metaphysics-institute, groundless-alignment, center-for-the-study-of-apparent-selves, perspectiva). 23 of the 40 entries are potential, and 19 transfer only by convening their own community.

openings.title: Professional mediators applying conflict transformation to the AI race
openings.summary: No one treats the frontier-lab race, or the hostility between the AI-safety, AI-ethics and accelerationist camps, as a conflict to analyse and mediate with peacebuilding methods. A small programme run by experienced mediators, starting with a conflict analysis and a camp-to-camp dialogue, would test whether those methods can lower the temperature where game-theoretic race models only describe it.
openings.detail: Peacebuilding's core tools (conflict analysis of actors, interests and positions; insider mediation; dialogue between parties who distrust each other) are absent from AI safety. The map shows this: there is no peacebuilding entry in core, and centre-for-humanitarian-dialogue is the only one in bridge, where it works on military AI between states. Berlin-based berghof-foundation holds these methods but has no AI work (transfer none_yet). cmi-martti-ahtisaari-peace-foundation has published AI principles for mediation, but it uses AI in peace processes rather than mediating AI's own conflicts. Industry forums coordinate the labs, but none is a mediated process, and int/a's principle of not making the race worse has no institutional home. Success in the first 18 months would be a published conflict analysis of the AI race written by mediators, plus at least one recurring, facilitated safety-ethics dialogue whose participants report better working relations. Risks: anything between labs needs antitrust counsel and must stick to safety topics. The conflict may not be ripe. Confidentiality also makes impact hard to show, which is the same problem safe-ai-forum and centre-for-humanitarian-dialogue already have.
steps: Commission berghof-foundation or cmi-martti-ahtisaari-peace-foundation to write a standard peacebuilding conflict analysis of the AI race (parties, interests, escalation dynamics, possible entry points), costed at a few months of mediator time.

int/a pilots a facilitated dialogue in Berlin or London between AI-ethics and AI-safety researchers, which carries lower stakes than working with the labs, and uses intelligence-rising's role-play to surface each side's assumptions.
Get antitrust advice and sound out lab policy and safety staff on a discreet Track 1.5 limited to safety topics such as incident sharing and red lines.
Have an outside peace researcher run a before-and-after evaluation, so the pilot's results can be read by funders outside the peace field.
openings.evidence: Peacebuilding is 11 of 51 peace entries, with 0 core and 1 bridge. berghof-foundation is the only peace entry tagged none_yet. The discovery notes, gap (a), found no one applying conflict transformation to the race between labs or between camps. Search for Common Ground and Beyond Conflict were checked and showed no AI engagement. A quick search for 2026 returned only work that uses AI in mediation (CSIS, CMI, Belfer), not mediation applied to AI.

openings.title: A standing STS observatory studying how AI-safety knowledge is made
openings.summary: STS and anthropology have studied how physics, biomedicine and climate science produce knowledge, but no organisation does this for AI safety: its evaluations, forecasts, safety cases and stories about the future. A small observatory would place ethnographers and controversy mappers alongside safety organisations and report back to the field, a direct answer to the narrowing the brief describes.
openings.detail: The scholarly interest exists. At 4S's 2026 meeting, 26 of 244 open panels had AI in the title, and EASST 2026 had at least 13 AI panels. But 4S, EASST and CASTAC sit in the potential ring with no AI programme, and EPIC, whose members are ethnographers inside companies, only convenes. The blind-spot sweep found no organisation whose main work is ethnography of AI labs or of the safety community, no history of AI-risk ideas, and no AI programme at Mellon, Wenner-Gren or the SSRC. The nearest efforts have ended or are narrow. Shaping AI has been dormant since February 2024, though its French team had begun work on a safety meme. The Cambridge Histories of AI seminar has closed. IAS's SINAI studies narratives of AI. The Computer History Museum's new AI Archive preserves records rather than analysing them. Sciences Po's médialab in Paris and the Weizenbaum Institute in Berlin have the methods and sit near int/a hubs. Success would be two or three embedded researchers publishing studies of evaluation validity, forecasting practice and safety-case culture that safety organisations actually use, plus a map of AI-risk debates updated each year. The risks: much critical STS rejects the x-risk frame, safety organisations may refuse access or treat the work as PR, and results come slowly. The observatory needs a host that both sides trust and a brief that does not instrumentalise the research.
steps: Run a small call through 4S and EASST for STS and anthropology researchers to spend 6 to 12 months embedded with willing safety organisations: evaluators, AISIs and forecasting groups.
Commission médialab, or the former Shaping AI team, to map AI-risk controversies with its digital methods.
int/a hosts an annual meeting where the findings go back to safety practitioners.
Ask Mellon or Wenner-Gren to co-fund, since neither has an AI programme.
openings.evidence: Five of the 8 law entries in the potential ring are STS or history bodies. The blind-spot sweep marked ethnography of the safety community 'thin', the history of AI-risk ideas 'thin', and humanities funders 'searched_none_found'. 4S and EASST panel counts as above. Shaping AI is dormant and Histories of AI is closed.

openings.title: Open catastrophe scenarios for correlated foundation-model failure, led by actuaries
openings.summary: Five actuarial bodies on the map run AI work, but all of it is about model governance and fairness. None applies the profession's methods for tail risk, accumulation and solvency to AI, even as insurers warn that reliance on three model providers makes agent liability behave like a catastrophe peril. An open set of disaster scenarios for foundation-model failure, built with the actuarial profession, would give AI safety a market-tested, priced view of correlated risk.
openings.detail: institute-and-faculty-of-actuaries, international-actuarial-association, society-of-actuaries-research-institute, casualty-actuarial-society and actuaries-institute are all adjacent and all frame AI as a present harm. The insurers price frequent, low-severity model error (armilla-ai, munich-re-aisure) or business-level risk (geneva-association). artificial-intelligence-underwriting-company is the exception: in September 2026 it proposed a mutual insurer for frontier labs. Outside the map, a quick search found the Lloyd's Market Association's first survey of AI loss scenarios (January 2026). It also found July 2026 notes from AIUC and the Cloud Security Alliance saying that over 80% of enterprise agent deployments run on three providers, which makes the risk an accumulation the market cannot yet price. So the commercial market has started. What is missing is a public scenario set backed by the profession, on the model of Lloyd's Realistic Disaster Scenarios, joined up with frontier-risk work: gradient-institute's 'monoculture collapse' failure mode, saferai's quantitative risk models, and bank-of-england and financial-stability-board's framing of frontier AI as a threat to financial stability. Success would mean an IFoA working party publishing open scenarios and accumulation measures that regulators use in stress tests and that labs' safety frameworks cite. The risks: insurers' commercial interests, scenarios that make extreme risk look insurable when the true tail cannot be priced, and a fast-moving commercial field.
steps: Propose an IFoA working party on catastrophic and accumulation risk from AI, building on the IFoA's September 2026 symposium and AI Manifesto.
Use int/a's London hub to convene IFoA, the Lloyd's Market Association, the Geneva Association, AIUC, Gradient Institute and Bank of England staff to agree three to five open scenarios.
Fund one actuarial researcher to cost the scenarios and publish the method and data.
Feed the results into SaferAI's risk models and CLTR's policy work, so frontier risk thresholds rest on a priced view of the tail.
openings.evidence: There are 5 actuarial bodies, all adjacent and all present-harms framed. The blind-spot sweep found 'no actuarial body working on catastrophic or long-horizon AI risk'. 4 insurers or insurance think tanks are on the map, only one of them frontier-explicit (AIUC). 5 of the 11 safety organisations in London are in finance, audit or actuarial work (IFoA, FCA AI Lab, IIA, ISACA, LRF).

openings.title: An epidemiology unit measuring AI harms at population level
openings.summary: Public health has the methods to tell whether chatbots and AI companions harm people at scale: surveillance, cohort studies, attributable-risk estimates and hazard classification. Yet no school of public health or national institute treats AI as an exposure. A dedicated unit would produce the population figures that company statistics and incident databases cannot give.
openings.detail: The safety_health sub-tradition has 10 entries and no core ones. Its AI-relevant work consists of single research lines inside other units. rand-health-care showed that published estimates of 'mental health use' of chatbots range from 0.01% to 72%, depending on definitions. flinders-health-and-medical-research-institute-f, a cancer-epidemiology lab, runs repeated audits of chatbot safeguards. department-of-affective-disorders-aarhus-univers uses health records. algorithmovigilance-programme-vanderbilt-univers monitors clinical models, and its founder left in September 2026. global-centre-for-preventive-health-and-nutritio has written one Lancet comment on chatbot advertising. The blind-spot sweep found no national public-health institute (RKI, RIVM, UKHSA, CDC and others) treating AI as a harm, no IARC-style hazard classification, and no WHO workstream on consumer chatbots. Papers now call AI a determinant of health, but nobody runs a programme on it. Success would mean a sentinel network of emergency and psychiatric services coding AI-associated presentations, an adolescent cohort study, and yearly attributable-risk estimates that regulators (us-fda-digital-health-advisory-committee) and labs can act on. The same surveillance machinery is early warning for slower, society-wide effects such as dependency. The risks: exposure is hard to define, data from companies is hard to get, and the work could feed a moral panic. It also overlaps with psychiatry groups such as stanford-brainstorm.
steps: Fund a three-year pilot unit at a school of public health that already has digital-epidemiology capacity.
Agree a standard definition of AI exposure with RAND Health and the Flinders group, so studies can be compared.
Set up a sentinel code for AI-associated presentations with a few emergency and psychiatric services, building on the Aarhus health-records method.
Negotiate privacy-preserving access to usage data with one chatbot provider.
openings.evidence: safety_health has 0 core entries and 10 in total. National public-health institutes were searched and none found working on this. The Flinders, RAND and Vanderbilt lines are each a strand of a non-AI unit. The safety-science notes list this as gaps (f) and (i). A quick check on 2026-10-04 found papers but no standing unit.

openings.title: Statisticians and metrologists set uncertainty reporting for dangerous-capability evaluations
openings.summary: Statistics and measurement-science bodies now run AI programmes, but all of them frame AI as sector regulation or present harms. Meanwhile, verdicts on whether a frontier model crosses a dangerous-capability threshold often rest on a few runs with no stated uncertainty. A secondment programme and a reporting protocol in the style of the GUM (the metrology Guide to the Expression of Uncertainty in Measurement) would bring their methods to the evaluations that trigger safety commitments.
openings.detail: The royal-statistical-society's AI Task Force has an evaluation subgroup and argues that regulating AI is largely a statistical evaluation problem. european-network-for-business-and-industrial-sta has a Reliability and Safety group and a 2027 meeting on design of experiments for AI validation. euramet-european-metrology-network-for-mathemati links 14 national metrology institutes. national-physical-laboratory opens its Centre for AI Measurement in November 2026, and ptb-competence-centre-ai-and-metrology already issues test-dataset specifications. NIST published a report on statistical models for AI evaluation (AI 800-3) in February 2026. None of these bodies works with uk-ai-security-institute or independent evaluators on the evaluations that decide whether a frontier model crosses a dangerous-capability threshold. Success would be a short, citable protocol for reporting uncertainty and traceability in such results, adopted by at least one AI safety institute and one developer. Risks: NIST and NPL may do this themselves, making an outside effort redundant; and the harder problem may be construct validity (does the test measure the risk?) rather than sampling error, which statistics alone does not fix.
steps: Fund three or four six-month secondments of industrial statisticians or metrologists, recruited through the RSS AI Task Force and ENBIS's Reliability and Safety group, into UK AISI or an independent evaluator.

Ask NPL's Centre for AI Measurement and PTB AI-Met whether frontier dangerous-capability evaluations are in their scope; if not, convene them with UK AISI to draft a GUM-style supplement for capability thresholds.
Re-analyse a handful of published dangerous-capability results with mixed-effects models to show how often a threshold verdict falls inside the error bars; this makes the case concretely.
openings.evidence: Statistics and metrology bodies make up four of formal's seven potential entries (american-statistical-association, european-network-for-business-and-industrial-sta, euramet-european-metrology-network-for-mathemati, international-society-for-bayesian-analysis), with royal-statistical-society in the bridge ring. All five are framed as present harms. blind_spots.md calls metrology for AI evaluation 'a clear blind spot'. The statistics sweep ran without web search, so recall is weak.

openings.title: Deep-uncertainty decision methods to stress-test frontier safety frameworks' if-then thresholds
openings.summary: Frontier safety frameworks rest on if-then commitments, which work like the signposts and triggers of adaptive planning, yet the decision scientists who built that method for flood defence and climate policy have no AI programme. A pilot would apply robust decision making, adaptive pathways and structured expert elicitation to one published framework.
openings.detail: The DMDU Society (society-for-decision-making-under-deep-uncertain) and the INFORMS Decision Analysis Society (informs-decision-analysis-society) hold the toolkit: dynamic adaptive policy pathways, robust decision making, value-of-information analysis and multi-attribute trade-offs. Both are in the potential ring and mention AI only in meeting themes. The discovery sweep found no structured-expert-judgement group (Cooke's Classical Model, IDEA, SHELF) working on AI. A few 2026 arXiv papers have started applying deep-uncertainty language to frontier AI policy, but no organisation owns the work. On the AI side, saferai already rates frontier frameworks, center-for-ai-risk-management-alignment works on risk management, and society-for-risk-analysis is a bridge. Success would be a published stress-test of one developer's thresholds across many plausible futures, showing which triggers fail and which signposts are missing, taken up in SaferAI's ratings or by an AI safety institute. Risks: developers may not disclose enough to make the analysis concrete; practitioners from climate and water may lack AI fluency and produce generic results; and a field that relies on forecasting may treat the work as redundant with probabilistic forecasts.
steps: Fund a six-month pilot pairing two DMDU practitioners (from the TU Delft or RAND lineage) with SaferAI to stress-test one published frontier safety framework.
Propose an AI track for the DMDU Society's 2027 annual meeting and a special issue of the journal Decision Analysis.
Run one structured expert elicitation on a dangerous-capability threshold using Cooke's Classical Model with calibration questions, and compare the results with forecasting-platform estimates.
openings.evidence: Both decision-science entries are in the potential ring with 'convening' transfer and no AI programme. blind_spots.md rates decision-analysis communities as thin and lists expert-elicitation communities as searched with none found. formal x epistemics has only four entries.

openings.title: Metacognition-science evals of model self-reports, built for both safety and welfare
openings.summary: Whether a model's self-reports track its internal states matters for AI welfare (self-reports as evidence) and for safety (honesty, sandbagging, situational awareness), but the work sits only in welfare groups. A small eval programme would pair human-metacognition and disorders-of-consciousness methods with evals organisations.
openings.detail: Introspection research on the map is entirely framed around welfare: eleos-ai-research (introspection, persona-dependent preferences), rethink-priorities (introspection, preference coherence), reciprocal-research (self-report, valence) and anthropic-model-welfare-programme. Human-metacognition researchers are arriving only as individuals. The May 2026 preprint 'Can LLMs Introspect? A Reality Check' applies criteria from human metacognition (privileged access, second-order computation) and finds that recent positive claims outrun the evidence. Disorders-of-consciousness medicine has decades of practice in assessing awareness without trusting behaviour: command-following imaging paradigms and perturbational complexity measures. A fellowship and an open benchmark run with uk-ai-security-institute would give safety evals a validated test of self-report, and give welfare work a shared standard of evidence. Risks: lab interpretability teams may get there first; training on such evals could teach models to perform introspection rather than have it; and better self-modelling tests overlap with dangerous situational-awareness capabilities.
steps: Fund a 12-month fellowship placing three or four metacognition psychophysicists (type-2 signal detection, confidence calibration) with UK AISI and Eleos. Megan Peters, already on the advisory boards of Conscium, PRISM and Harder Problem, is a natural first contact.
Build an open benchmark on open-weight models in which interpretability supplies ground truth for privileged-access tests, and publish what training on it does to scores.
Run a two-day workshop with disorders-of-consciousness clinicians to adapt self-report-independent paradigms to AI systems.
Recruit through neuromatch's AI Sentience Scholars to reach researchers outside the US and UK.
openings.evidence: Only 3 of 28 minds organisations code 'assurance' (eleos-ai-research, conscium, anthropic-model-welfare-programme). None codes security, multi_agent, power or systemic. The neuro angle notes say that 'no one runs introspection and metacognition evals with evals orgs'. Disorders-of-consciousness or anaesthesia research appears nowhere in index.txt.

openings.title: Structured adversarial collaboration on AI consciousness, co-funded by Templeton
openings.summary: AI-welfare work rests mostly on computational functionalism. The rival theories are held by mainstream consciousness scientists who sit at the edge of the field, and all the funding comes from a few EA sources. An adversarial collaboration on specific AI architectures, run with a non-EA science funder, would test the field's foundations and widen its money and its geography at once.
openings.detail: Templeton World Charity Foundation's $30M Accelerating Research on Consciousness initiative already runs pre-registered adversarial collaborations between theories (IIT vs global workspace, first-order vs higher-order, IIT vs predictive processing). A quick search found none on artificial systems. The John Templeton Foundation launched a $60M+ 'Future of Intelligence' venture on 3 Oct 2026. rethink-priorities' Digital Consciousness Model already combines 13 theoretical perspectives, but with weights chosen by experts. association-for-mathematical-consciousness-scien's MoC7 (Copenhagen, 12–16 Oct 2026) plans a consensus paper on LLMs, and ASSC meets in Beijing in 2027. Success would be a funded project with pre-registered, theory-specific predictions about named architectures (a transformer LLM, a recurrent agent, a neuromorphic system like those at conscium or araya-inc), whose results update the DCM's weights. Risks: some theories, IIT in particular, may give verdicts set by hardware that can't be tested, and the results could be used to legitimise deliberately building conscious systems, the stated aim of california-institute-for-machine-consciousness and Araya.
steps: Use MoC7 in October 2026 to recruit a team spanning at least three camps: functionalist or global-workspace, IIT, and biological naturalist (Sussex/Seth). Add one non-Western group (NIAS) and one phenomenological group (Copenhagen CFS).
Draft a two-page concept note for TWCF's consciousness programme, presenting RP's DCM as the outlet that turns results into updated estimates.
Ask Longview to co-fund a small share, so the result has credibility in both funding pools.
Hold one adversarial workshop beside ASSC 2027 in Beijing to bring in Chinese consciousness scientists.
openings.evidence: All five minds entries with a 'critical' framing (sussex-centre-for-consciousness-science, center-for-consciousness-studies-the-science-of, qualia-research-institute, essentia-foundation, center-for-subjectivity-research-university-of-c) sit outside core, and all 11 core entries are welfare-led. The funders named across the minds profiles are Navigation Fund, Polaris/Macroscopic, Longview, SFF, Coefficient Giving and EA Funds. Eight entries disclose no funder. There are no entries in Africa, Latin America or MENA, and only 2 in Asia-Pacific.

openings.title: An ecology lab for populations of deployed AI agents
openings.summary: Large numbers of interacting AI agents are now deployed, yet nobody studies them as populations: what selection pressures act on them, how conformity cascades form, and when an agent ecosystem tips. Collective-behaviour biologists, evolutionary game theorists and cultural evolutionists already have these tools. A dedicated lab, partly staffed from Konstanz's collective-behaviour cluster as its funding ends, would apply them.
openings.detail: Konstanz's CASCB (more than 160 researchers) published work in August 2026 showing that capable LLM agents coordinate by following the majority in groups far larger than humans manage. The cluster was not renewed in the May 2025 Excellence Strategy decision, so its funding runs out in 2027 and skilled people will be looking for a home. MPI Plön and IT:U Linz (Hilbe: LLM strategies in the repeated prisoner's dilemma), Teesside (Han: evolutionary game theory of AI races), MPIB's Center for Humans and Machines (machine behaviour) and the Cultural Evolution Society (no AI activity, though members co-wrote 'Machine Culture') hold complementary methods. The tradition's multi-agent work in core and bridge either builds models (Softmax, XOR Labs) or simulates (Concordia, Equilibria); none observes real deployed populations. The Cooperative AI Foundation, which funds multi-agent risk research, is a natural co-funder. Success would be population-level monitoring of real agent ecosystems, early-warning indicators of cascades, and an ecology-grounded taxonomy of multi-agent failure. The risks: platforms control access to deployment data, there is overlap with cooperative-AI groups, and the analogy can stretch too far (agents are copied, not bred), so the lab must test which biological mechanisms actually hold.
steps: Talk to CASCB's leadership and David Garcia's group about which researchers face the 2027 funding end and would join an AI-agent-populations project.
Seek co-funding from the Cooperative AI Foundation and SFF for a two-year pilot of four to six researchers.
Propose an applied working group on machine culture to the Cultural Evolution Society, which invites proposals for new working groups.
Negotiate data access with at least one agent platform or marketplace before hiring.
openings.evidence: centre-for-the-advanced-study-of-collective-beha and max-planck-institute-for-evolutionary-biology-de are potential, and cultural-evolution-society is none_yet. In life x multi_agent, the 4 core and 4 bridge entries are model-builders or simulators, there are 0 adjacent entries, and the 2 potential entries are the Konstanz and Plön groups above. CASCB's funding ends in 2027. A web search for ecology of AI agents returned only AI-for-ecology work.

openings.title: Mediators and negotiation scholars co-building evaluations for AI-agent conflict
openings.summary: The peace x multi_agent cell is empty, even though conflict between agents is the peace field's core subject and AI agents are starting to bargain and escalate against each other. A research programme pairing professional mediators and negotiation scholars with cooperative-AI researchers would turn concepts such as ripeness, face-saving and third-party mediation into tests of how AI agents escalate and settle conflicts.
openings.detail: Multi-agent AI is the least-covered problem on the whole map (34 entries, 14 primary), and the discovery notes say peace-and-conflict researchers and mediators are absent from AI–AI conflict, with CLR almost alone. Cooperative-AI groups on the map (foundations-of-cooperative-ai-lab, witt-lab-university-of-oxford-moving-to-ucl, modeling-cooperation, equilibria-network) and the Concordia simulation library work mostly from game theory and computer science. Practitioner knowledge sits in geneva-centre-for-security-policy (its PIN negotiation programme, not yet applied to AI), cmi-martti-ahtisaari-peace-foundation and centre-for-humanitarian-dialogue. The democracy notes add a second gap: no one systematically red-teams AI mediators (habermas-machine is dormant). Success would be an open evaluation suite that tests whether LLM agents recognise deadlock, take face-saving exits, accept a mediator's single negotiating text, or escalate, developed by mixed teams of mediators and researchers. Risks: mediators' skill is largely tacit and may not translate. Better negotiating agents are also a capability, so evaluations should measure escalation and failure to settle rather than train agents to win.
